title: Leptospirosis (infection from animal urine or floodwater)

items: Leptospirosis is an infection spread by the urine of infected animals, often through water or wet soil.
It usually starts 5 to 14 days after exposure.
Fever, headache, and muscle pain in the calves and back.
Red eyes (conjunctival suffusion) and sometimes jaundice (yellow skin).
Leptospira antibody tests (IgM ELISA or MAT).
Kidney and liver function tests, blood count, clotting tests, and creatine kinase (CK).
Your doctor will decide on antibiotics, and fluids or dialysis if the kidneys are affected.
Some people need admission and close monitoring.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Tell your doctor if you have been in floodwater or in contact with animals.
Avoid swimming in stagnant water while you are unwell.
Kidney and liver tests may be repeated to check recovery.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.
